title: Wren and the Horizon
premise: August Whitlock, a disgraced railroad engineer, is hired to trace a vanished government survey team along the closed mountain lines on their old map — only to discover the team was hunting a wrecked supply train sealed inside a glacier since the war. Racing a salvage fleet that wants the wreck's rumored gold bullion, August must navigate six tides of open passage before calving season seals the route for another year. Betrayed by an ally who serves the salvage fleet's corrupt financier, August reaches the wreck first but must choose between claiming the inheritance that would restore their name and destroying the pass to keep it out of corrupted hands; they collapse the ice tunnel with the gold inside and walk out owning nothing but the truth — and, at last, belonging among the valley people who helped them.
about_author: Coral Thornbury is the pen name of a former surveyor's assistant who spent four seasons mapping high-altitude rail corridors before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about landscapes that keep secrets, drawing on a family archive of railroad ledgers and expedition letters.

chapters.title: The Map of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: August Whitlock, POV. Broke and blacklisted after a bridge failure blamed on them, August takes a courier job delivering sealed orders to a remote survey station. The chapter establishes the compass inherited from their father, the debt, and the map of lines officially closed. Emotional beat: restless shame, hunger for one chance at redemption.

chapters.title: Gear With No Tracks
chapters.summary: August, POV. Arriving at the station, August finds it abandoned mid-meal: instruments laid out, a fire cold, no footprints beyond the door. A dying signal lamp still ticks. The local telegraph operator, Sera Voss, insists no team ever arrived. Emotional beat: creeping dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Sera, POV. Sera explains the glacier route opens only during low-water tides before calving season — six tides, then sealed. A salvage fleet under financier Aldous Crane is already provisioning at the port. August realizes the vanished team found something worth killing for. Emotional beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: The Last Open Line
chapters.summary: August, POV. August and Sera board a handcar up the closed line, passing sabotage — rails spiked, culverts blown — done recently and expertly. Someone wants the route unusable except to those who know it. August recognizes the engineering hand: their old mentor, Halvard. Emotional beat: unease turning personal.

chapters.title: The Valley That Remembers
chapters.summary: Sera, POV. In a valley settlement off the maps, the pair find shelter with Ilsa Brandt, whose grandfather drove trains through the pass. She reveals the wrecked supply train carried not just supplies but the region's seized gold, lost when officials scuttled it to hide embezzlement. Emotional beat: first taste of belonging.

chapters.title: Halvard's Ledger
chapters.summary: August, POV. Following Halvard's trail markers, August finds his camp — abandoned like the survey team's — and his ledger proving the bridge failure that ruined August was engineered to cover Crane's cost-cutting. August was framed. Emotional beat: fury and vindication entwined.

chapters.title: First Tide
chapters.summary: August, POV. At the glacier mouth as the first tide drains, the ice tunnel stands open — a cathedral of blue. Inside: fresh boot prints, spent flares, and a surveyor's badge. The team went in and never came out. Distant engines announce the salvage fleet has reached the valley. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by pursuit.

chapters.title: What the Ice Keeps
chapters.summary: Sera, POV. Deep in the tunnel, they find the survey team — alive, trapped behind a collapse, rationing lamp oil. Their leader, Okafor, refuses rescue until they log what they found: the wreck, and evidence of who sank it. Emotional beat: relief curdling into moral complication.

chapters.title: Crane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Okafor, POV. Flashback chapters within Okafor's account: Crane offered the team a fortune to certify the wreck as derelict so salvage rights would transfer to him. When Okafor refused, Crane's men sealed them in. Emotional beat: the corruption's scale revealed.

chapters.title: Second Tide
chapters.summary: August, POV. Hauling the weakened team out costs precious hours; two tides are gone. Salvage scouts reach the tunnel mouth and a standoff ends in a truce neither side trusts. Halvard appears among Crane's men — changed, hollowed. Emotional beat: exhaustion and wary negotiation.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Confession
chapters.summary: Halvard, POV. By firelight, Halvard admits he falsified the inspection reports that doomed August's bridge, believing Crane's promises, then watched the pass become a grave. He gives August the original wreck manifest — proof of the embezzlement. Emotional beat: grief, guilt, a fragile alliance.

chapters.title: Third Tide
chapters.summary: Sera, POV. The truce breaks: Crane's foreman tries to seize the manifest, and in the scramble Okafor is injured. Sera leads the group through a crevasse field only she can read, buying a tide's lead. Emotional beat: fear mastered into competence; trust forged.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: August, POV. Camped at the wreck itself — a locomotive frozen mid-flight — August reads the manifest: the gold was public funds, stolen from these very valleys. It isn't treasure; it's restitution owed. Emotional beat: the theme lands — inheritance as obligation, not windfall.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide
chapters.summary: Ilsa, POV. Ilsa arrives overland with valley volunteers carrying blasting powder from the old works. Crane's full fleet unloads at the mouth. Both sides dig in for the last usable tides. Emotional beat: the valley chooses its side; August stops being alone.

chapters.title: The Financier Ascendant
chapters.summary: Crane, POV. Crane's chapter reveals his philosophy: money is the only law left, and whoever holds the gold holds the valleys. He offers August full pardon and reinstatement in exchange for the manifest. Emotional beat: seduction of power, and August's quiet refusal forming.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide
chapters.summary: August, POV. The fifth tide opens and both parties race the tunnel. Crane's crew blasts a shortcut, destabilizing the ice. August reaches the wreck's strongroom as cracks spider overhead. Emotional beat: desperation, physical peril, the route literally closing.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Strongroom
chapters.summary: Halvard, POV. Halvard betrays Crane — locking the strongroom gate against the salvage crew — and is shot for it. Dying, he tells August the gold isn't worth the tunnel's life: the calving will bury everything anyway. Emotional beat: sacrifice, forgiveness asked and given.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide
chapters.summary: August, POV. Climax. With the final tide draining, August triggers the old charges and collapses the tunnel — sealing the wreck, the gold, and Crane's claim beneath a thousand tons of ice. Crane, caught inside his own shortcut, is lost. August barely escapes as the glacier calves. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into choice.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Ice
chapters.summary: Sera, POV. The fleet retreats leaderless. Okafor's testimony and Halvard's ledger go to the magistrate; the bridge inquiry reopens and August's name is cleared. The gold remains buried — unrecoverable, but documented, its theft on record. Emotional beat: justice incomplete but real.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: August, POV. Quiet aftermath: funerals for Halvard and the valley's losses, August repairing the closed line not for profit but to reconnect the settlements. Ilsa offers work; Sera offers company. Emotional beat: grief settling into gratitude.

chapters.title: The Compass Points Home
chapters.summary: August, POV. August finally understands the father's compass — its needle fixed not north but toward the pass. Some inheritances aren't claimed; they're answered. August signs on as the valley line's engineer. Emotional beat: peace earned, identity rebuilt.

chapters.title: Wren and the Horizon
chapters.summary: Sera, POV. Epilogue, spring. A wren nests in the restored station eaves; the horizon road runs open again. A letter arrives: Crane's empire is under investigation, and other sealed lines want engineers. August looks down the track and smiles. Emotional beat: forward motion — the story ends where belonging begins.
